Absorption Speed, New Site Speed, Dose Interaction, CGM Lag and Micro-doses

How many times faster or slower than standard your infusion site absorbs insulin, once the site has settled (from 48 hours after a site change). Only the absorption from the site changes: the insulin\'s time in the blood and the delay to its effect are your body\'s and stay as they are. 1: as in the pump study the model is fitted to, on day 3 of the infusion set.

How fast a new infusion site absorbs, as a share of a settled site\'s speed. Right after a site change the site absorbs at this share of Absorption Speed, and it reaches full Absorption Speed 48 hours later, as from day 1 to day 3 of the pump study the model is fitted to. 0.49: that study\'s day 1 against its day 3. 1 turns this off.

The share of every dose that absorbs together with all insulin at the injection site and is slowed by it: boluses, SMBs, extended boluses and basal, temp basals included. The rest of each dose absorbs on its own. 0 turns this off: no insulin interacts with any other, and every dose, each minute of basal included, absorbs on its own. 1: all insulin follows the same path, absorbing at the pace set by all insulin at the injection site.

Model every bolus and SMB the way your pump delivers it: in small pulses at its bolus speed, instead of all at once. Each minute of pulses joins the insulin at the injection site together, and the part of each pulse that Dose Interaction leaves out absorbs on its own, as fast as a lone pulse, so below a Dose Interaction of 1 boluses absorb faster than without this. A bolus still counts whole as insulin on board from when it starts. Basal is unchanged. Turning this on changes the insulin curves: you may need a lower Absorption Speed or a higher Dose Interaction.
The insulin your pump gives in one pulse during a bolus, for example 0.05 U.
How fast your pump gives a bolus, in units per minute: 1.5 U/min is one 0.05 U pulse every 2 seconds.

How many minutes your CGM trails your blood glucose. Every dose\'s activity is delayed and smoothed by about this much, so it lines up with the glucose changes your CGM shows, and the part of the effect the CGM hasn\'t shown yet still counts as insulin on board. Includes your sensor\'s own smoothing. The model\'s delay from insulin in the blood to its effect was fitted together with 8 minutes here. 0 turns it off.
